Horadric Odds

D2R drop calculator
Welcome to Horadric Odds — a free, fan-made, all-in-one toolkit for Diablo II: Resurrected.
  1. Drop odds: search any item (nicknames like "shako" work) to see which monsters drop it and your chance per kill at your difficulty, players and magic find.
  2. Build planner: open Share & Library, pick a starter build or make your own, and spend points on Skills & Stats.
  3. Play it: the Leveling Guide has a checklist to tick off while you level, and Gear shows where to farm each item. Experience shows the fastest places to level.
  4. Tools: track your Holy Grail and runs, see what your runes make, check rolls and cube recipes, and edit offline characters with the Save editor.

      How the odds are worked out

      How it works. Odds are calculated from the game's own drop tables (treasure classes, monster levels, item ratios), following the in-game rules: NoDrop scaling by player count, the level-based treasure class upgrade in Nightmare and Hell, nested picks with the 6-item limit per kill, the quality roll with diminishing magic find, and unique/set selection by rarity. Chances are per kill. With Find Item they're per successful search. Stat rolls: every value in a stat's range is equally likely; magic and rare affixes follow the game's affix level, weights, group and prefix/suffix rules.

      Game versions. D2R Reign of the Warlock (current), D2R before the expansion (patches 2.4 to 2.9) and Lord of Destruction 1.14d (same drop tables as 1.13c). Classic LoD tables come from the game's 1.14d patch files; item and skill names are shared with D2R.

      Compared with Silospen. Same maths: regular monsters, cows and champions match exactly. Checked against all three of its game versions. Bosses at 1 player and the Countess's runes differ because Silospen approximates the 6-items-per-kill limit (it counts only 6 of a boss's 7 picks and doesn't limit nested picks), while this calculator applies the limit as the game does.

      Gambling follows the rules published on Blizzard's Arreat Summit (item level, upgrade chances, fixed quality odds); the elite upgrade is assumed to be checked before the exceptional one.

      Sharing. The page's link keeps the item, stats and settings you picked, so copying it shares your exact calculation.

      Not modelled. The once-per-game unique rule, scripted drops (Cow King hide, organs from Uber events, Hellfire Torch, Annihilus) and super uniques without a fixed location. Heralds are assumed to get the same +3 level bonus as unique monsters.

      How it works

      Experience follows the game's rules: monster base experience by level, the player count bonus (+50% per extra player), the party bonus and level-based split, the level difference penalty, the high-level reduction from level 70 and the 8,388,607 per-kill cap. Champions give 3× (berserkers 5×), uniques, minions and super uniques 5×. Monster counts per area (regular monsters, champions, uniques and their minions, with separate counts for terror zones) come from u/Pavke's Experience Calculator, which covers Hell; Nightmare uses the same monsters with its own number of elite packs, and Normal Act V keeps its own monster mix scaled to his totals. Treat clears as averages. Baal's five waves are counted, but each wave is treated as its boss plus that boss's minion type, so the Throne numbers are close rather than exact. Not counted: monsters that appear mid-fight (Fallen revived by Shamans, Vile Children from Vile Mothers and the like), because how many you get depends on how you play, and the one-time reward from the Ancients quest, since it can't be farmed. Data from blizzhackers/d2data (MIT); rules checked against The Amazon Basin wiki. Big thanks to u/Pavke on Reddit, whose Experience Calculator supplies the monster counts and was used to check every number here.

      How to use Horadric Odds

      Horadric Odds is an all-in-one toolkit for Diablo II: Resurrected, worked out from the game's own data. There's nothing to install or sign up for, it works on PC and phone, and everything you save stays in your browser.

      Drop odds

      Build planner

      Drop odds

      1. Find the item. Type its name in the search box. Nicknames work too: shako, soj, anni, griffs. Uniques, sets, runes and bases are all there. Pick a runeword to see where to farm each of its runes.
      2. Set up your game. Pick the difficulty, how many players are in the game, how many party members are near you, and your magic find (the 0, 300 and 500 buttons are shortcuts). Tick Area is terrorized for a terror zone, Find Item corpse for a Barbarian's Find Item, or First boss kill for a quest drop.
      3. Read the results. Every monster and area that can drop the item, best first, with your chance per kill shown as “1 in N” kills.

      Other ways to search

      By stats
      Pick the stats you want and the lowest value you'd accept, e.g. +2 skills and 20% FCR. You'll see which items can roll them and where to find them.
      By monster
      Pick a boss, super unique or monster type to see everything it can drop.
      Gambling
      Your odds of gambling a specific item, or stats you want, at your character's level.
      Merchants
      Your odds of a merchant selling an item with the stats you want, e.g. a 4-socket body armor with +100 life. Pick the merchant, difficulty and your level; each base shows its own chance, and hovering a base shows its best magic rolls.

      Tip. The page's link keeps the item and settings you picked, so you can copy it to share your exact calculation. Turn on diablo2.io price links at the top to get a price check link for the item in your market.

      Build planner

      1. Start a build. Open Share & Library and pick a guide build for your class, or choose a class at the top and start from scratch. Give it a name and a target level.
      2. Spend skill points on Skills & Stats. Click a skill, or its + button, to add a point. Its − button removes one (or right-click on PC). Shift-click adds or removes up to 20. Missing prerequisites are added for you, and the order you click is the order the leveling guide spends points. Hover over a skill (press and hold on a phone) to see its in-game tooltip: damage at your level and the next, synergies, masteries and, for attack skills, your damage with the weapon you've planned.
      3. Set your stats with the + and − buttons next to Strength, Dexterity, Vitality and Energy. Hold Ctrl for steps of 5, or Shift for steps of 10.
      4. Plan respecs with + Respec at a level. Each phase has its own skills and stats, e.g. a leveling build until 75 and an endgame one after that.
      5. Plan your gear on Gear. Click an empty slot to pick from the items that fit there (search by name or nickname). For a runeword you choose the base, sockets and ethereal; for a charm or rare you can enter its stats. Click any item to pick it up and click where it should go, like in the game; right-click an item to change or remove it. To add to the inventory, right-click an empty space or use + Add to inventory. Charms in the inventory count toward your totals, and other gear can be stored there. Pick your mercenary from the Mercenary menu at the top of the Equipment panel; it sets the merc's aura and is used when you export the build. Hover or tap an item for its stats and requirements.
      6. Gear counts once you can wear it. An item only adds to your life, resistances, breakpoints and other totals from the level you meet its required level, Strength and Dexterity (your other gear's bonuses count, its own don't). Requirements you haven't met show in red, and the leveling guide lists each item at the level you can really put it on, or says when a build can never wear it.
      7. Follow the leveling guide. Leveling Guide lists every level: which skill to put the point in, stats, new gear, life and mana. Tick levels off as you play and add your own notes.
      Compare
      Two builds side by side at their target levels, with their full gear.
      Share & Library
      Save builds in this browser, copy a build code to post on Discord, Reddit or a forum, or paste someone's code into Import to load their build. The code carries skills, stats, respecs, gear and notes.
      Import save
      Load an offline character's save file (.d2s) to open its build in the planner with its skills, stats and gear, tick everything it owns in your Grail, and count its runes. Add your shared stash (.d2i) too. The file is read on your device and never uploaded. Online characters can't be imported.
      Export Build
      Turn the build into an offline character: pick the phase to export (the final one unless you choose another), choose the save version and name, tick the quests, acts and difficulties it should have done (the default follows its level), and create it in the save editor. Its skills, stats, gear and mercenary are put on the character; gear it can't use yet goes on anyway and the game shows it red. For offline characters only.

      Keep your build codes. Saved builds live in this browser only. If you clear your browser data or switch devices, they're gone, so copy the code somewhere safe.

      Experience

      1. Enter where you are. Your level, how far through it you are (the % from your experience bar), and a goal level if you have one.
      2. Pick how far you've got under Furthest you've reached, so it only suggests areas you can actually get to. Then set the difficulty, players, party size and any experience bonus such as a shrine.
      3. Read the results. Experience left, plus kills and full clears to your next level and your goal. Areas are ranked by experience per clear, and you can tap one to see what's worth killing there.
      4. Follow the route. With a goal level set, you get a suggested route of areas to level in. It only moves forward through the difficulties and sticks to areas you've unlocked.

      Tip. Tick Terror zones only to rank terrorized areas, which get higher monster levels and +25% experience.

      Tools

      Holy Grail
      Tick every unique, set item and rune as you find it, and watch your progress by type. Filter by armor, weapons or jewelry and by tier, or show only what you're missing. Every item has an odds button that shows where it drops.
      Runes
      Enter the runes you own. You'll see which runewords you can make right now, which ones you could make after cubing runes up (with the exact cube steps and gems), and which ones you're one rune short of. Search by name, nickname (cta, coh, hoto, infy), rune or item type to see what any runeword needs.
      Run tracker
      Pick a boss or super unique, press +1 run after each run and log what drops. A timer gives your runs per hour, and your drops are compared with the drop calculator's odds, so you can see whether you're lucky or the farm just isn't worth it.
      Farm planner
      Add several item goals, including runewords (which become rune goals), then choose a boss or super unique. Set how many you already have, how many you want, kills per run and your run time to estimate expected drops and the runs needed for a 50% or 90% chance of finishing the full list. Completion estimates are approximate.
      Roll checker
      Pick a unique, set item or runeword and type in your item's numbers to see how good each roll is, from 0% (lowest) to 100% (perfect), plus an overall score.
      Sockets & affixes
      Pick a base and its item level to see how many sockets Larzuk or the cube can give it, and which magic or rare affixes can roll on it, e.g. whether a grand charm can roll +1 skills. Affixes that need a higher item level are listed with the level they need. Crafted items work out their item level from your character level.
      Save editor
      Load an offline character (.d2s from D2R, Lord of Destruction 1.14d or Classic 1.14d) to change its level, stats, skills and gold, move, copy or delete items, and add any unique, set item, runeword, rune or gem, or a magic or rare item with the affixes you pick. Tick the quests, acts and difficulties it has completed on Quests. You can also create a fresh character from a planned build (Build planner → Export Build). Download the edited save and put it in place of the old one. Back up the original first.
      Cube recipes
      Every Horadric Cube recipe from the game files: rune and gem upgrades, sockets, item upgrades, crafting, rerolls and uber keys. Search by any ingredient.

      Back up your data. Your builds, checklists, Grail, runes, farm plans, runs and settings are saved in this browser. Open Tools → Backup & restore to download one backup file or move your data to another device.

      Questions

      How do I see a skill's details?
      In the build planner, hover over a skill in the tree (press and hold on a phone). The tooltip shows the game's description, damage at your level and the next, synergies, mastery bonuses and, for attack skills like Zeal or Whirlwind, your damage with the weapon you've planned.
      How do I see an item's stats?
      Hover over an item's name anywhere on the site, or tap it on a phone. Uniques, set items (with their set bonuses), runewords (including each rune's own bonus) and runes all show their stats as the game words them.
      Which game version does it use?
      D2R Reign of the Warlock by default. Drop odds can also use D2R before the expansion or classic Lord of Destruction 1.14d. Choose with Game version.
      How accurate are the numbers?
      Drop chances come straight from the game's drop tables and rules, and they've been checked against other calculators. They're averages, so luck still decides any single run. How each tool works is explained at the bottom of its page.
      Can I link someone straight to a tab?
      Yes. Add #planner, #experience, #grail, #runes, #runs, #cube, #editor, #import or #how-to-use to the address, e.g. horadricodds.github.io/#how-to-use. A drop odds link already carries the item and settings you picked.
      Can I use it offline or install it like an app?
      Yes, on horadricodds.github.io. Once you've opened the site, it works without an internet connection. To install it: on a phone, use your browser's menu and choose Add to Home Screen (or Install app); in Chrome or Edge on PC, use the install icon in the address bar. It updates itself whenever you're online.
      Where is my stuff saved?
      Settings, saved builds, leveling ticks, your Grail, runes, farm plans and run trackers stay in your browser on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere. Use Tools → Backup & restore to download all Horadric Odds data as one file and restore it on another device.
      The page looks out of date.
      Your browser may be showing an old copy. Press Ctrl+F5 on PC, or pull down to refresh on a phone.
      Something's wrong, or I have an idea.
      Use Something wrong? Report it at the bottom of any page. It opens a GitHub issue with your version, tab and settings already filled in, so you only need to say what happened. You can also open an issue yourself or email HoradricOdds@hotmail.com. Include the item or build, your settings, and what you expected.
      About & credits

      Horadric Odds is free and fan-made. It isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard Entertainment, Maxroll, IGN, Icy Veins or diablo2.io. Diablo II: Resurrected and its game data belong to Blizzard Entertainment. The site is open source under the MIT License.

      Game data: items, drop tables, skill trees and formulas come from the game files via blizzhackers/d2data (MIT License, © 2020 blizzhackers).

      Experience: rules checked against The Amazon Basin wiki; monster counts per area come from u/Pavke's Experience Calculator (thanks, Pavke!), which was also used to check the numbers. Attack frames: animation frame data and timing rules follow Warren1001's IAS Calculator (animation tables dumped by RuffnecKk). Cast, hit-recovery and block breakpoints: d2runewizard, with the Warlock tables confirmed against AOEAH.

      Builds: starter builds are written for Horadric Odds from the game data and common community knowledge. Full guides by Maxroll and Icy Veins are linked from each build and from the Guides list. Community builds belong to the players who share them.

      Save files: the save format comes from the community's reverse engineering (d07riv, dschu012/d2s (MIT), nokka/d2s, krisives/d2s-format, and the d2s Rust crate for Reign of the Warlock). Lord of Destruction and Classic tables come from the 1.14d game files.

      Prices: the optional price links open diablo2.io's price check for the item, with permission from its admin. Horadric Odds doesn't collect or store any price data.

      Artwork: item pictures from LootCube; the inventory panel texture from Dimentio’s D2R UI assets. Diablo II: Resurrected artwork belongs to Blizzard Entertainment; Horadric Odds does not own or claim rights to it and is not affiliated with Blizzard or LootCube.

      Bugs and ideas: open an issue on GitHub or email the address below.

      Contact, problems or takedown requests: email HoradricOdds@hotmail.com, or use Report on any shared build.
